name: Kamiokande
full_name: Kamioka Nucleon Decay Experiment / Kamioka Neutrino Detection Experiment
summary: The original Kamioka water Cherenkov detector began as a nucleon-decay experiment and became a landmark instrument for supernova, solar and atmospheric neutrino physics.
detection_principle: Large photomultipliers recorded Cherenkov light patterns in ultrapure water. Upgraded shielding and timing lowered backgrounds sufficiently to observe MeV-scale neutrino interactions.

sites.name: Japan; underground in the Kamioka mine, Gifu Prefecture
sites.location: Japan; underground in the Kamioka mine, Gifu Prefecture

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The observatory lists Kamiokande as the historical 1983–1996 detector.

timeline.event: Low-energy refurbishment for solar-neutrino observation completed; data taking resumed.
Main data taking ended as Super-Kamiokande began.

collaboration.name: Kamiokande Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Water tank
key_parameters.value: Approximately 3,000 tonnes of water in the tank; surrounding cavern water definitions differ

key_parameters.name: Inner photomultipliers
key_parameters.value: 948 50-cm PMTs in the official historical comparison

key_parameters.name: Underground location
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1,000 m below the mountain at Kamioka

results.summary: Detected a neutrino burst from SN1987A, providing direct experimental evidence for neutrino emission in stellar core collapse.
Directional solar-neutrino observations and atmospheric flavour studies broadened its legacy.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
